title: The proper-base-change dictionary
statement:
The spectral sequence statements used in the proper-base-change chapter are
read with the following substitutions. For a scheme $X$, the abelian category
[def-sp-abelian] $\mathcal A$ is the category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ of abelian
sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], which is
Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For a morphism
$f:X\to Y$, the left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor
$v$ is the etale direct image $f_*:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image], with right derived functors $R^nf_*$. A
bounded-below complex $K^\bullet\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\Ab(X_{\Et}))$
represents an object $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$
[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; its K-injective resolution supplies
the computation of $Rf_*K$ [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. The functors
$\Phi$ occurring in the base-change comparisons are $Rf_*$,
$Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, and $g^{-1}Rf_*$, where the inverse images on derived
categories are [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. For a cartesian
square, the natural transformation used to compare the resulting couples
is the derived exchange morphism
$\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]; its compatibility with the couple
structure is a separate statement. For composable morphisms
$X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$, the composable pair
[def-sp-composite-acyclicity] $(F,G)$ is $(f_*,h_*)$.
